# Sources and terms

Authored fan internals: Psych0h3ad. Authored routing, parameters and numerical centreline sources: CORE One Community Guide contributors. Authored code is MIT; authored geometry, model parameters and numerical model data are CC BY-SA4.0. Preserve attribution and the applicable share-alike terms when distributing adapted model data.

Three.js, copyright2010–2024 Three.js authors, is distributed under MIT; its full notice is in `licenses/THREE-MIT.txt`. NumPy and cadquery-ocp are external build dependencies and are not bundled here.

Reference sources:

- [Prusa CORE One CAD](https://www.printables.com/model/1520471): existing fan-frame envelope and assembly registration. Native frames are outside this package and retain their source Open Community License.
- [Chamber fan replacement, guide944814](https://help.prusa3d.com/guide/how-to-replace-the-chamber-fan-core-one_944814): assembly sequence, seven-blade appearance and front/rear orientation; steps966134 and969929.
- [Back assembly, step985751](https://help.prusa3d.com/guide/3-back-assembly_982260#985751): fan orientation.

Official text, photographs and third-party CAD retain their own terms. This package contains links to those references and independently authored model inputs; it contains no supplier STEP, supplier mesh faces or official photograph copies. The rear label is neutral.

The eight conductor lengths are authored material references, not manufacturer cut-length measurements. The retained curve coordinates are editable numerical model inputs. The manifest's opaque compatibility identifiers describe its existing data format; they are not additional files required to build the model.
